name: Chateau La Cheneviere
insider_take: This 18th-century Norman manor house sits majestically on 12 acres of manicured parkland, just minutes from the legendary D-Day beaches where history was made.
whats_special: The château features original period furnishings and tapestries, while its Michelin-starred restaurant showcases authentic Norman cuisine using ingredients from their own kitchen garden. The property's unique position offers panoramic views over the Seulles Valley, and many rooms overlook the English Channel where Allied forces landed in 1944.
pro_tip: Book the "Liberation Suite" – it's where General Montgomery himself stayed during the Normandy campaign, and it includes private access to the château's historic war room with original maps and artifacts.
dont_miss: The château's private World War II bunker tour (available by appointment), afternoon tea in the orangery overlooking the rose gardens, and the 10-minute drive to Omaha Beach for sunset – one of the most moving experiences in France.
pros: Historic 18th-century chateau with authentic French architecture and period furnishings
Prime Normandy location near D-Day beaches and historic sites
Elegant fine dining restaurant featuring local Norman cuisine and exceptional wine selection
Beautifully landscaped gardens and peaceful countryside setting
cons: Remote countryside location requires transportation for local exploration
Historic property with traditional room layouts and period-style amenities
